pr_title: Respect `ANSIBLE_HOME` when determining SSH control path directory
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

When choosing the default `control_path_directory` for SSH connections, Ansible will now respect the `ANSIBLE_HOME` configuration setting, instead of using a hardcoded `~/.ansible`.

Because this new behavior relies on a value from `ansible.constants`, I've removed the default for this variable from the docstring, in favor of calculating it in Python at the point of use.

Fixes #79737.

##### ISSUE TYPE

<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->

- Bugfix Pull Request

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

When running the repro steps from the original issue, with the `-vvv` option, the new control path can be seen in action:
```
<citadel.local> SSH: EXEC ssh -C -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=60s -o KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no -o PreferredAuthentications=gssapi-with-mic,gssapi-keyex,hostbased,publickey -o PasswordAuthentication=no -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o 'ControlPath="/Users/sodle/.cache/ansible/cp/c8e8ca50e5"' citadel.local '/bin/sh -c '"'"'rm -f -r /home/sodle/.ansible/tmp/ansible-tmp-1697684386.315946-8679-39523000970181/ > /dev/null 2>&1 && sleep 0'"'"''
```

issue_context.title: `control_path` default for `ssh` connection plugin does not respect `ANSIBLE_HOME`
issue_context.body:
### Summary

When using the copy module, it creates `$HOME/.ansible/cp` not honouring the configured `$ANSIBLE_HOME`

```
export ANSIBLE_HOME=$HOME/.cache/ansible
```

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

copy

### Ansible Version

```console
$ export ANSIBLE_HOME=$HOME/.cache/ansible

$ ansible --version
ansible [core 2.14.1]
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/simon/.cache/ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /home/simon/.cache/ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.11.1 (main, Dec  7 2022, 00:00:00) [GCC 12.2.1 20221121 (Red Hat 12.2.1-4)] (/usr/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.0.3
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
$ export ANSIBLE_HOME=$HOME/.cache/ansible

# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
ANSIBLE_HOME(env: ANSIBLE_HOME) = /home/simon/.cache/ansible
CONFIG_FILE() = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
```


### OS / Environment

Fedora release 37 (Thirty Seven)


### Steps to Reproduce

⚠️ 

```
export ANSIBLE_HOME=$HOME/.cache/ansible

mv $HOME/.ansible $HOME/.ansible.bak
touch /tmp/foo
ansible server.example.com -m copy -a 'src=/tmp/foo dest=/tmp/foo' --check

stat $HOME/.ansible
find $HOME/.ansible

### Expected Results

`$HOME/.ansible` does not exist

### Actual Results

```console
> find $HOME/.ansible
/home/simon/.ansible
/home/simon/.ansible/cp
/home/simon/.ansible/cp/912df56293
```
```

The ssh plugin uses `control_path_dir` , which defaults to `~/.ansible/cp`, while we do have a global config that uses `$ANSIBLE_HOME/cp` that does not affect the ssh connection plugin.

review_comments: one thing that troubles me ... the user has no way to use ``ANSIBLE_HOME`` themselves except by accepting the default ... should this wait until we make the options templatable and grant access to the constants?

Updated code in both places.

As for holding this change back until options are templatable... I think that makes sense for consistency: the fact that there is confusion around how to refer to a constant in documentation, feels like a symptom of that inconsistency.

I'll leave that decision to the people who understand the project roadmap better than I do. However, I'd be happy to contribute to the templatable options effort, if I'm able.
